# Embedded C++ Code in a Quarto book {.unnumbered}
This example uses:  
[Miniforge](https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge) as an installer for  
[Mamba](https://github.com/mamba-org/mamba) as a package manager so  
[xeus-cling](https://github.com/jupyter-xeus/xeus-cling) can run C++ through  
[JupyterLab](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab) under the hood, and  
[Quarto](https://github.com/quarto-dev) can compile it into an HTML page

Below is a demonstration of some C++ code followed by a Jupyter shortcut.  
Omitting the semi-colon will simply print the value of what is written  
```{cpp}
int i = 10;
i
```

### This is another embedded code example that is a *little* more involved
```{cpp}
#include <iostream>

std::cout << "Hello from xeus-cling";
```

#### The bits of embedded code are very clearly best intended to be small demo code segments instead of full blown assigment vectors.
